options.counterfactual: Every normalized 2-quasitrace sends the successive differences of a bounded increasing positive sequence to zero, even if that sequence has no least upper bound.
options.approach: Seek a finite-family packing estimate: for each positive epsilon, bound the number of positive elements with quasitrace at least epsilon whose sum is at most the identity. Such an estimate would immediately exclude the prescribed constant increments.

options.counterfactual: Every normalized 2-quasitrace sends the successive differences of a bounded increasing positive sequence to zero, even if that sequence has no least upper bound.
options.approach: Look for a state that controls the quasitrace through a nonlinear inequality on positive contractions. Applying the state to bounded positive partial sums could then force their individual quasitrace values to vanish.

options.counterfactual: Every normalized 2-quasitrace sends the successive differences of a bounded increasing positive sequence to zero, even if that sequence has no least upper bound.
options.approach: Investigate whether failure of exhaustion produces an ultraproduct containing ordered positive elements with identical spectral distributions but a nonzero difference. Seek a contradiction using the quasitrace axioms rather than assuming strict order preservation.

options.counterfactual: The finite AW*-factor hypotheses imply that every bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements has a least upper bound.
options.approach: Audit the precise monotone sequential completeness theorem, including its hypotheses and its distinction from projection-lattice completeness. A verified theorem applying here would exclude every witness independently of the quasitrace.

options.counterfactual: The finite AW*-factor hypotheses imply that every bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements has a least upper bound.
options.approach: Try to construct the supremum using spectral cutoffs and joins of projections. The central task would be proving that the resulting element lies above the entire noncommuting sequence and below every upper bound.

options.counterfactual: The finite AW*-factor hypotheses imply that every bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements has a least upper bound.
options.approach: Investigate a dilation of the increasing positive sequence to increasing projections in an enlargement of the algebra. Determine whether projection suprema in that enlargement can be compressed back into the original factor.

options.counterfactual: Whenever a finite AW*-factor has a nonlinear faithful normalized 2-quasitrace, it contains a sequence satisfying all the requirements for some positive eta.
options.approach: Start from a positive additivity defect and investigate whether equivalent corners allow it to be repeated while keeping positive partial sums bounded. Then use interpolation to make the quasitrace increments exactly constant.

options.counterfactual: Whenever a finite AW*-factor has a nonlinear faithful normalized 2-quasitrace, it contains a sequence satisfying all the requirements for some positive eta.
options.approach: Study whether nonlinearity forces finite positive families with sum at most the identity and arbitrarily many quasitrace values bounded away from zero. An ultraproduct could turn such finite families into an infinite sequence.

options.approach: Separate the construction of constant increments from the absence of a least upper bound. Investigate whether order continuity at an existing supremum would rule out that supremum for any sequence produced from persistent additivity defects.
